title: Air Conditioning Leads: How AC Companies Get More (2026)
summary: How AC companies get air conditioning leads from Google, Meta and local ads, with real ad patterns, cost per lead math and a simple plan.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Air conditioning leads come in four types: emergency repair, tune-up, system replacement and air quality or duct work. Each needs its own offer and its own ad.
- Google Search and Local Services Ads catch people whose AC just stopped. Facebook and Instagram fill the schedule with tune-ups, duct cleaning and financing offers before and after the hot weeks.
- The ads on the[air conditioning ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/air-conditioning-ads) that run longest are simple: one service, one price or discount, one action.
- Measure cost per booked job, not cost per click, and answer every lead within minutes.


## Air conditioning leads are four different kinds of buyer


Air conditioning marketing fails when one ad tries to speak to everyone. A homeowner whose unit quit at 2 p.m. on a 98 degree day wants a truck today. A homeowner thinking about a new system wants a number and a payment plan. A homeowner who sees a tune-up ad in April is not in a hurry at all. The offer, the channel and the follow-up change for each.


Lead type What the buyer wants Best channel Offer that fits


Emergency repair Cold air today, from someone who answers the phone Google Search, Local Services Ads, Google Business Profile Same-day service, upfront diagnostic fee


Tune-up and maintenance A fair price, no surprise, before summer Facebook and Instagram, email to past customers Seasonal tune-up price, maintenance plan


System replacement A firm quote, a brand they trust, a monthly payment Google Search, Facebook lead ads, retargeting Free in-home estimate, financing


Duct and air quality Cleaner air, lower dust, a visible reason to act Facebook and Instagram, video Percent off duct cleaning, air quality check


If you also handle heating, the broader[HVAC marketing guide](https://www.sprites.ai/hvac-marketing) covers the furnace side of the year.


## What the ads that keep running have in common


The[air conditioning ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/air-conditioning-ads) shows 381 live Meta ads from 60 advertisers. About 40% of them are video. The typical ad has run 24 days, which tells you most are swapped out within a month. The most common call to action button is Learn more, on about 28% of ads.


The ads at the top of the longevity list are more useful than the average. The longest ones have run between 491 and 1,147 days. Four patterns show up.


1. **One plain offer.** An ad that opens with "10% Off Residential DUCT CLEANING" has run 617 days. There is nothing to decode. The service, the discount and the customer type are all in the first line.
2. **A question about the home.** "Is the air inside your home polluted or dirty?" has run 491 days. It starts with a problem the homeowner can picture.
3. **Air quality and duct work, not only repair.** Several of the longest-running ads sell duct cleaning, ductwork replacement or indoor air. These jobs do not depend on a heat wave, so the ads can run year round.
4. **Trust and a local reason to respond.** Others lean on decades in business, a Facebook-only special with savings of up to $100, or a promise of service the customer has not had before. Video appears in several of them.


What this shows is not that discounts beat everything. It shows that the ads advertisers leave on for years name a specific service and a specific benefit, and ask for one action. Ads built around a vague brand claim tend to be replaced.


## Where air conditioning leads come from


### Google Search


People type "AC not cooling", "air conditioner repair near me" and "AC replacement cost" when they need help. This is the highest-intent traffic you can buy. Build separate campaigns for repair and replacement so you can set different budgets. Repair clicks cost more but close faster. Replacement clicks bring bigger tickets.


### Local Services Ads


Pay-per-lead listings sit above the regular search results, with a verification badge. Eligibility and screening depend on your category and location, so check Google's requirements. Our[Local Services Ads guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) walks through setup and how to dispute poor leads.


### Google Business Profile


Keep hours accurate, add photos of your trucks and installs, and ask every customer for a review. In a heat wave, the profile with 200 reviews and a phone number that gets answered gets the call.


### Facebook and Instagram


Meta works best for demand you create: tune-ups before summer, duct cleaning, maintenance plans and financing on a new system. Use lead forms with questions such as system age and home size, or send clicks to a short landing page. See[Facebook ads for HVAC companies](https://www.sprites.ai/facebook-ads-for-hvac-companies) for how these campaigns are set up.


### Your own customer list


Past customers are the cheapest air conditioning leads you will ever get. Send a text or email in spring offering a tune-up, and again when their system passes 10 years old.


## Sample ads by lead type


Replace the town, the price and the proof with yours. Only run an offer you will honor.


### Emergency repair (Google Search)


- Headline:` AC Repair in Phoenix Today` (24 characters)
- Headline:` Same-Day Service Available` (27)
- Headline:` Licensed and Insured Techs` (27)
- Description: "AC stopped working? Call now and a licensed technician can be at your door today. Upfront pricing, no surprise fees."


### Tune-up (Facebook and Instagram)


"Summer hits fast. Book your AC tune-up now for $89 and make sure your system is ready before the first 100 degree day. We check refrigerant, coils, capacitor and airflow, and tell you what we find in plain language." Button: Book now.


### Replacement (Facebook lead form)


"Is your AC over 12 years old? Get a free in-home estimate and see what a new system costs per month with financing. No pressure. Most visits take about an hour." Form questions: system age, home size, how soon.


### Duct and air quality (video)


A 20 second clip of a technician pulling dust out of a vent, followed by: "Is the air in your home as clean as it looks? 10% off duct cleaning for homeowners this month."


## The math behind a lead


Count what a lead costs and what it returns. Here is a worked example with assumed numbers. Replace them with your own.


Step Repair campaign Replacement campaign


Monthly ad spend $2,000 $1,500


Cost per lead $50 $75


Leads 40 20


Booked visits (60% and 50%) 24 10


Jobs won (70% and 40%) 17 4


Average ticket $450 $9,000


Revenue $7,650 $36,000


Cost per job won about $118 $375


The replacement campaign costs more per lead and per job, yet it produces more revenue per dollar, because one install pays for many clicks. This is why you should not judge campaigns by cost per lead alone. Look at the cost per job won against your gross profit on that job.


## Answer speed decides who wins the lead


Someone with a broken AC calls two or three companies and books the first that picks up. Missed calls are lost jobs. Three habits protect your ad spend:


- Answer live during business hours, or use an answering service after hours.
- Text back any missed call or form fill within five minutes.
- Keep call tracking on every ad so you know which campaign produced which job.


If your lead cost looks fine but jobs are few, the gap is almost always here.


## Plan the year around the heat


- **Spring.** Run tune-ups and maintenance plans. Demand is not yet urgent, so prices are lower.
- **Summer.** Shift budget to emergency repair on Google and Local Services Ads. Raise bids when forecasts show a heat wave.
- **Early fall.** Run replacement and financing offers when homeowners have just survived a hard summer with an old unit.
- **Winter.** Sell duct cleaning and air quality, which the longest-running ads on the wall do year round.


Other trades keep a similar calendar, and the[AI ads for local service businesses](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/ai-ads-for-local-service-businesses) post shows how to adjust budgets across a year.

## FAQ


### How do I get more air conditioning leads?


Start with Google Search and a complete Google Business Profile for people who need help now. Add Facebook and Instagram for tune-ups, duct cleaning and financing offers. Answer every lead within minutes and track which source produces booked jobs.


### What is a good cost per lead for AC companies?


It depends on your market, season and lead type. Repair leads often cost less than replacement leads, but replacement leads return more per job. Compare cost per job won with your gross profit on that job instead of chasing the lowest lead cost.


### What offers work best in air conditioning advertising?


The ads on the wall that run longest use a plain offer: a percent off duct cleaning, a seasonal tune-up price, same-day repair or financing on a new system. Name one service, one benefit and one action.


### Should AC companies use video ads?


Video is common, with about 40% of the ads on the wall using it. A short clip of a technician at work, a before and after of a dirty duct or the owner speaking directly works well. A clear photo still beats a vague video.


### Are Facebook ads or Google ads better for air conditioning leads?


Google catches people searching for repair right now. Facebook and Instagram create demand for tune-ups, duct work and replacements before the need is urgent. Most AC companies do best using Google for emergencies and Meta for planned work.
